sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r10/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: Quality Checks row 6 and Internal Quality Checks row 6 (internal wording still says 'no network'; public sheet and SKILL.md delivery profile say public network is allowed, applied the public wording)

.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r10/rules/projects/webdev-task-template/instruction.md, environment/instructions/*.md; template tests/test.sh, tests/Dockerfile and environment/Dockerfile compared byte-for-byte with the task (identical)

task/solution/solve.sh, solution/app/package.json, solution/app/static/runner.html, solution/app/src/runtime.ts (instrumentation, CSP and rejection handling, lines 1-90 and grep hits), solution/app/server.js (grep hits)
evidence: REACHABILITY (holds). instruction.md:3 says 'six notes in /instructions' and environment/instructions holds exactly six files, copied by environment/Dockerfile:14; /assets/seed_data.json exists (Dockerfile:15) and matches 'no starter app' (seed_data.json:2-3). integration.md:5 'The launch image supplies Node 22, Express and better-sqlite3 through NODE_PATH' is true in both images: environment/Dockerfile:1,3,9-11 and tests/Dockerfile:1,9,20-21 pin the same node:22-bookworm-slim, express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1, and tests/test.sh:104-111 launches with that NODE_PATH. integration.md:3,9,11 (cwd may be outside /app, DB_PATH, writable copy, symlink rule) describe test.sh:72-83 and 97-111 accurately, so no launch condition is hidden. Network is public (task.toml:22,38), so a formatter/parser (policy.md:3, ui.md:15) and a test browser are obtainable. The hard capabilities have a known browser-only route: sandboxed iframe plus CSP for security.md:3-5, loop/timer instrumentation for the five-second budget and Stop (behaviour.md:5-7), Intl.Segmenter for ui.md:5 graphemes. The golden does exactly this (solution/app/src/runtime.ts:7 CSP with connect-src 'none' and worker-src 'none'; runtime.ts:33-76 acorn instrumentation; runtime.ts:376 sandbox='allow-scripts'), and the scripted golden run on these exact bytes, installed with solve.sh in the agent image and launched as uid 65534 with env -i, reports every one of the 3 gate, 42 functional and 6 polish ids true with no page errors (results/editor.json, runtime.json, polish.json, persist-before.json, persist-after.json; all 22 index hashes recomputed and equal). I found no requirement that needs anything outside seed, runtime or public internet. ONE READING (holds for the graded behaviour). I tried the alternative 'a tab with no unsaved edits auto-loads the newer revision', which would make cw_stale_save_refused and cw_stale_save_keeps_draft unproducible (functional/judge.toml:353,362 have A save first and B edit afterwards); behaviour.md:11 rules it out unconditionally ('That refresh must not touch what I'm doing: the draft ... stay as they were' and 'do not load the newer revision over my work') and behaviour.md:9 states the old-revision Save must fail, so that app is non-conforming, not a second reading. Thresholds in criteria are looser than the brief (ten seconds against 'about five', judge.toml:299,380), never stricter. MINOR ITEMS REPORTED (none shown to misgrade a conforming app): (1) behaviour.md:3 asks for 'a one-based line number ... for a Promise rejection that nothing handles; the message is the text of the Error or rejected value'. For a rejected non-Error value the browser's unhandledrejection event carries no line, so this is reachable only through source instrumentation or promise tracking (golden: runtime.ts:46-48,114,229). The criterion only uses new Error (judge.toml:245), so nothing ungradeable is graded, but the brief literally promises more than the platform gives cheaply. (2) behaviour.md:3 says 'one-based line number' for an error inside a complete HTML file without saying counted from the first line of the file; judge.toml:236 fails a count from the start of the script block. File-relative is the natural reading, script-relative is a weak second one. (3) ui.md:9 'Undo and Redo controls are disabled whenever there is nothing for them to do' does not say that New or opening a snippet starts a fresh history; polish/judge.toml:50 assumes it ('Load a saved snippet or start a new draft so there is no editing history'). An app that lets Undo take back a New would be marked down; a fresh page load avoids it. (4) behaviour.md:5 'until that run settles' leaves a legitimately endless setInterval or animation page classed as over budget after five seconds; this is one reading and consistent with judge.toml:281,299, only worth stating as intended. (5) overview.md:3 does not say what a filename that is neither .js nor .html does; not graded. NOT MEASURED: no configured judge run and no target-model build exists for these bytes (raw-evidence-index.json:3,43-45); the hosted run was an earlier candidate, where the only model build scored 0. So achievability is shown for the reference solution under scripted checks only, not for an agent inside the 7200 s budget (task.toml:18) and not under the real judge's browser (for example clipboard behaviour of an app that uses the async clipboard API instead of copy/paste events). That gap is why risk stays true.
suggested_fix: Optional hardening, no blocker: in behaviour.md say the HTML line is counted from the first line of the file and limit the rejection line number to rejections that carry an Error; in ui.md say a new or freshly opened snippet starts with an empty Undo history (or make cw_undo_redo_availability use a freshly loaded page). Any such edit creates a new candidate and needs re-review.
